evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1996-005
evidence.claim: In 1996, chloride testing for AF-12 was introduced because ammonium chloride additions could cause under-film corrosion.
evidence.quote: the ammonium chloride addition (CR-1995-009) introduces chloride, which can promote corrosion under the film.

evidence.title: Laboratory report LT-2020-044 - chloride and drying study, AF-12
evidence.claim: In 2020, under-film corrosion complaints on AF-12 were investigated, confirming chloride levels originate from the ammonium chloride addition.
evidence.quote: investigate two complaints of under-film corrosion on AF-12 coated steel (2019). Chloride content of 20 production batches: 380-420 ppm

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1995-009
evidence.claim: In 1995, ammonium chloride was added to AF-12 to prevent livering caused by high alkalinity in Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti's CL-77 pigment.
evidence.quote: Reason: livering of AF-12 caused by the high free alkalinity of chromate pigment CL-77 supplied by Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1995-009
evidence.claim: The addition of ammonium chloride in 1995 was intended to be temporary until the supplier met alkalinity specifications.
evidence.quote: Duration: temporary - to be reviewed when the supplier delivers pigment within the 0.30 % alkalinity specification.

evidence.title: DEVIATION REPORT DR-1995-031
evidence.claim: In 1995, AF-12 batches suffered from livering (rubbery gel formation) after storage, leading to customer returns.
evidence.quote: tins opened after 4 to 6 weeks of storage show the enamel thickened into a rubbery gel ("livering")

evidence.title: DEVIATION REPORT DR-1995-031
evidence.claim: In 1995, livering in AF-12 was suspected to be caused by high alkalinity in Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti pigment lots CL-77/95-09 and CL-77/95-10.
evidence.quote: Suspected cause: reaction between the acid groups of the alkyd and the basic lead chromate pigment

evidence.title: LABORATORY TEST REPORT LT-1995-118
evidence.claim: In 1995, lab tests showed that CL-77 pigment lots 95-09 and 95-10 exceeded alkalinity specifications, causing AF-12 to gel during storage.
evidence.quote: Free alkalinity (as PbO): lot 95-07 0.21 %; lot 95-09 0.92 %; lot 95-10 0.88 %. Supplier specification: max 0.30 %.

evidence.title: LABORATORY TEST REPORT LT-1995-118
evidence.claim: In 1995, ammonium chloride was recommended as a corrective measure to neutralize excess alkali in the pigment and prevent livering.
evidence.quote: Recommendation: add 0.8 kg ammonium chloride per 1000 kg batch as a corrective measure while the supplier brings the pigment back

evidence.title: LABORATORY TEST REPORT LT-1995-118
evidence.claim: In 1995, it was noted that the addition of chloride to prevent livering could potentially impact corrosion protection.
evidence.quote: The effect of the added chloride on corrosion protection must be watched.

evidence.title: Laboratory report LT-2020-044 - chloride and drying study, AF-12
evidence.claim: In 2020, lab tests confirmed ammonium chloride does not affect drying and levels above 300 ppm contribute to under-film corrosion.
evidence.quote: ammonium chloride has no measurable effect on drying. Chloride above 300 ppm can contribute to under-film corrosion on steel.

evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2007-002 - Fosfazinco Nord S.p.A., ZP-40
evidence.claim: In 2007, the ZP-40 pigment was approved for AF-12, and trials showed the ammonium chloride addition was no longer needed.
evidence.quote: Trial T3 was prepared without the ammonium chloride addition and behaved like T1 and T2.

evidence.title: FATTURA / INVOICE n. 4638/01
evidence.claim: Ammonium chloride was still being purchased in large quantities in 2001.
evidence.quote: Item: Ammonium chloride technical, bags 25 kg. Quantity: 24,000 kg.

evidence.title: Response to complaint on CL-77 lots 95-09 and 95-10
evidence.claim: In 1995, Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti corrected the CL-77 process to ensure free alkalinity was 0.25% or less from February 1996 onwards.
evidence.quote: The process has been corrected. All lots from 96-02 onwards are released with free alkalinity of 0.25 % or less

evidence.title: Compliance memo CM-2006-004: phase-out of lead chromate pigments
evidence.claim: In 2006, the lead chromate pigment CL-77 was replaced by zinc phosphate ZP-40, with the final delivery of CL-77 in October 2006.
evidence.quote: basic lead chromate CL-77 will be replaced by zinc phosphate ZP-40 from Fosfazinco Nord

evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2007-002 - Fosfazinco Nord S.p.A., ZP-40
evidence.claim: In 2007, trials with ZP-40 pigment showed that AF-12 remained stable without the addition of ammonium chloride.
evidence.quote: Trial T3 was prepared without the ammonium chloride addition

evidence.title: QC RELEASE PLAN - QP-02 Batch QC release
evidence.claim: The chloride test for AF-12 batches with a 400 ppm limit was formalized in the QC release plan in 1996.
evidence.quote: Chloride on every AF-12 batch, max 400 ppm (see CR-1996-005).

evidence.title: QC RELEASE PLAN - QP-02 Batch QC release
evidence.claim: The chloride test was added to the AF-12 quality plan in 1996 following change request CR-1996-005.

evidence.title: QC RELEASE PLAN - QP-02 Batch QC release
evidence.claim: The chloride test for AF-12 remained in the QC release plan as of October 2003.
evidence.quote: Chloride on every AF-12 batch, max 400 ppm (see CR-1996-005).

evidence.title: QC RELEASE PLAN - QP-02 Batch QC release
evidence.claim: The chloride test for AF-12 remained in the QC release plan as of November 2009.
evidence.quote: Chloride on every AF-12 batch, max 400 ppm (see CR-1996-005).

verdict.instruction: Chloride content of every AF-12 batch (limit 400 ppm).
verdict.reason: The test was introduced to monitor corrosion risks caused by ammonium chloride additions used to prevent livering (E1, E3). While the original pigment causing livering was replaced by 2007 (E14, E15), a 2020 investigation confirmed that chloride levels above 300 ppm still contribute to under-film corrosion on steel (E10), and complaints occurred when levels reached 380-420 ppm (E2).

chain.claim: Ammonium chloride was added to AF-12 to prevent livering caused by high alkalinity in CL-77 pigment
Chloride testing was introduced to monitor under-film corrosion promoted by these additions
CL-77 pigment was replaced by ZP-40 by October 2006
Trials showed ammonium chloride was no longer needed with ZP-40
2020 reports confirm chloride levels above 300 ppm still cause under-film corrosion on steel

dependencies.name: ammonium chloride addition causing under-film corrosion
dependencies.note: Hazard persists if chloride is present, regardless of the original reason for adding it.

counter_evidence.claim: Ammonium chloride addition was no longer needed after switching to ZP-40 pigment
counter_evidence.resolution: The need for the additive ended, but the hazard of chloride (from any source) causing corrosion remains a quality risk.

open_questions: Is ammonium chloride still being added to the process for any other reason since 2007?
